newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW-Mexico consumption on the rise.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Mexico consumption on the rise.

text.p: Private consumption in Mexico appears on the rise and may have replaced the dynamic export sector as the engine of economic recovery, economists said on Friday.
Private consumption grew 3.2 percent during the first nine months of the year, according to figures from the Finance Ministry released on Friday.

"These are positive figures. What it shows is that internal demand is causing economic growth right now and not the external sector. The export stimulus is ending," said Alfredo Thorne, chief economist for JP Morgan in Mexico.
According to Thorne, private consumption grew 5.4 percent during the third quarter alone.
Another economist, Gene Frida at I.D.E.A. in New York, said the rise in consumption shows it is catching up to the rest of the economy.
"The retail sales figures and the rebound in consumer good imports were also evidence of a recovery," Frida said.

The Finance Minsitry also said gross capital formation rose 13 percent during the first nine months compared to a similar period the year earlier. Thorne said investment is growing even more than consumption.
Some economists questioned the government's use of nine-month figures for demand and not quarter alone data.
"I want to see the figures from the government to see if consumption really rose that much," a Mexico City-based economist said.
